newsitem.title: USA: Gateway gets boost from end of UPS strike.
newsitem.headline: Gateway gets boost from end of UPS strike.

text.p: Shares of Gateway 2000 Inc rallied sharply on news that United Parcel Service, one of its main shippers, had reached a contract agreement with the Teamsters union that would end a 15-day-old strike, traders said Tuesday.

"I think the stock's being pumped up because of the end of the UPS strike," said a Gateway options trader at the Pacific Exchange. "They ship everything through UPS, so this was perceived as certainly a positive for them."
At about 1120 CDT/1620 GMT, Gateway was up 2-1/2 at 39-3/4 on consolidated volume of more than 1.7 million shares.
UPS and the Teamsters union reached a tentative contract accord late Monday. UPS chief executive James Kelly said the company would begin returning to full operations Wednesday.

Traders also said Gateway, a major computer maker and direct marketer, was probably getting a boost from optimism in Dell Computer Corp, which is scheduled to report fiscal second quarter earnings after today's market close.

"With this UPS thing out of the way and Dell earnings coming out, I think people are willing to put their feet back into Gateway," an options trader in Chicago said. "That's why it's particularly explosive today."
